The sequence is defined by the rule that each term is the product of the number and the sum of its digits. This can be expressed recursively as follows:

### **Recursive Formula:**

For all integers $ n \geq 0 $:

$$
\text{term}(n) = 
\begin{cases}
n^2, & \text{if } n < 10 \\
n \times \left( (n \mod 10) + \text{sum\_of\_digits}(n \div 10) \right), & \text{if } n \geq 10
\end{cases}
$$

Where the **sum of digits** is defined recursively:

$$
\text{sum\_of\_digits}(n) = 
\begin{cases}
n, & \text{if } n < 10 \\
(n \mod 10) + \text{sum\_of\_digits}(n \div 10), & \text{if } n \geq 10
\end{cases}
$$

---

### **Explanation:**

- **Base Case (n < 10):**  
  For single-digit numbers, the sum of digits is the number itself, so $ \text{term}(n) = n \times n = n^2 $.

- **Recursive Case (n ≥ 10):**  
  For numbers with two or more digits, the term is calculated as:
  $$
  \text{term}(n) = n \times (\text{last digit} + \text{sum of remaining digits})
  $$
  This is achieved by taking the last digit ($ n \mod 10 $) and recursively computing the sum of the remaining digits ($ n \div 10 $).

---

### **Example:**

For $ n = 24 $:

- $ \text{sum\_of\_digits}(24) = 2 + 4 = 6 $
- $ \text{term}(24) = 24 \times 6 = 144 $

This matches the pattern in the sequence.

---

### **Final Answer:**

$$
\boxed{
\text{term}(n) = 
\begin{cases}
n^2, & \text{if } n < 10 \\
n \times \left( (n \mod 10) + \text{sum\_of\_digits}(n \div 10) \right), & \text{if } n \geq 10
\end{cases}
}
$$
